dedupe_keys.name: predicting thermal comfort in buildings with machine learning and occupant feedback

description: Skaloumpakas, Panagiotis and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The completed ASM headquarters application combines indoor/outdoor temperature observations with occupant questionnaire feedback. Neural networks forecast temperatures one hour ahead, and classifiers then estimate occupants' thermal sensations for HVAC or natural-ventilation decisions. The source reports testing and validation at the headquarters, but its abstract gives no numeric prediction score, occupant count or exact period. The case supports assessment of feedback-informed building-energy and comfort control. It is not treated as evidence that a controller was autonomously operated for an entire year or that every office had equivalent observations. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; a paper licence does not establish a software licence. Coverage is limited to the stated sites, model settings and application examples. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected. Linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
